Google-hosted mail (aspmx.l.google.com + smtp.google.com, 865 domains) is 100.0% PQ; everything else is 6.8% of completed handshakes (101/1489) / 5.7% of all MX domains (101/1768). Do NOT describe this as "on par with" the UK paper's 6.4% SMTP figure -- the UK's own 6.4% is itself ~98.4% Google-driven (per the UK paper's own stated attribution), so it is just as single-provider-dominated as ours, and the UK paper does not publish a non-Google rate to compare against directly. The defensible claim: both studies' national SMTP PQ figures are dominated by the same Google effect, not broader sector-wide modernization. See phase_d_baseline_comparison_report.md and PLAN.md Section 4.14/4.15 for the full breakdown. Do not cite the unstratified 41.0%/36.7% figure alone as a comparison point.
